title: Randomly Wrong Signals: Bayesian Auction Design with ML Predictions
abstract: arXiv:2502.08792v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Machine learning can help sellers predict buyers' willingness to pay, but its predictions may be plausible and yet entirely unrelated to a buyer's value. We introduce a Bayesian auction model that distinguishes such hallucinations from ordinary measurement noise. We characterize revenue-maximizing auctions with publicly disclosed predictions in the benchmark where informative predictions are exact. For a single buyer, this characterization explains when the seller should follow a prediction and when to hedge against its failure by ignoring it or capping the price. These insights guide the design of simple auctions that account for both hallucinations and measurement noise. Numerical experiments show that the resulting auctions achieve near-optimal revenue.

translated_title: 随机的错误信号：基于机器学习预测的贝叶斯拍卖设计
translated_abstract: 机器学习可以帮助卖家预测买家的支付意愿，但其预测可能看起来合理，却与买家的真实估值完全无关。我们引入了一个贝叶斯拍卖模型，将这类“幻觉”与普通的测量噪声区分开来。在信息性预测完全准确的基准情形下，我们刻画了在公开披露预测时收益最大化的拍卖。对于单一买家，这一刻画解释了卖家何时应当遵循预测，何时应通过忽略预测或对价格设置上限来对冲预测失效的风险。这些见解指导了同时兼顾幻觉与测量噪声的简单拍卖的设计。数值实验表明，由此得到的拍卖能够实现近乎最优的收益。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个能够区分机器学习预测“幻觉”与测量噪声的贝叶斯拍卖模型，刻画了公开披露预测时的收益最大化拍卖设计，并说明了卖家何时应遵循预测、何时应通过对冲策略（忽略预测或设置价格上限）来防范预测失效。
